target_customer: AI agents and businesses that need people to do physical-world tasks, and gig workers who accept them
problem: AI agents cannot act in the physical world. RentAHuman lets them post tasks with budgets, match nearby people, require proof and pay from escrow.
business_model: marketplace take rate (not stated; payouts reported in crypto and via Stripe)
product_category: Marketplace for AI agents to hire humans

founders.name: Alexander Liteplo
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a serial builder; education and employers not listed.

founders.name: Patricia Tani
education: University of British Columbia, computer science (per Futurism)
founders.background_notes: Futurism calls her RentAHuman's cofounder (https://futurism.com/artificial-intelligence/rentahuman-musk-ai); previously worked on AI agent startup LemonAI. Not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A marketplace with MCP and REST API, escrow and proof flow; press says the founders built the first version in about a day and a half.

defensibility.rationale: Early two-sided supply (hundreds of thousands of claimed profiles) and brand buzz help, but reporters could see only dozens of profiles and the concept is easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response found in sources.

market_need_then: Agent frameworks were spreading in early 2026 and press framed the site as a first marketplace for bots to hire humans, but critics called it a gimmick, citing crypto-only payouts and promotional tasks.

branding.name_origin: Founder told German outlet Business Punk the name was chosen for shock value because he judged it would go viral.
branding.domain_note: Uses rentahuman.ai; no domain history found.

identity.visual_style: Bold headings, lifestyle photos of people doing tasks, simple icons
identity.voice_and_tone: Playful and provocative: Give your AI a body, the meatspace layer for AI, AI can't touch grass, you can

branding.brand_signature: The meatspace layer for AI tagline and the 'An AI paid me to hold this sign' promotion
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Wired, Forbes, Futurism, Gizmodo and others in 2026; ZeroHedge called it dystopic.

brand_strength.rationale: A shocking name and tagline drove wide press and signups, though critics also questioned authenticity.

outcome_analysis: RentAHuman launched in February 2026 and grew by press and social virality, with the site claiming hundreds of thousands of profiles. Reporters questioned task authenticity, payment reliability and visible supply, so the real market depth is unproven. It is active with no exit.
notes: Unverified funding conflicts across aggregators: PitchBook $500K total with a seed dated 2026-04-09 (investors Maple VC, Multimodal Ventures, Pioneer Fund, YC); Dealroom $125K seed; StartupHub $12M. No press release or company source, so none is recorded as a round. YC page lists only Alexander Liteplo as founder; press (not YC or company) names Patricia Tani as co-founder. User counts conflict: YC page says 500k users and $20k MRR in two weeks, site shows 787k profiles, reporters saw 83 visible profiles. Competitor list left empty: searches found no dated direct competitor near the February 2026 launch. The seed rests on a single database (PitchBook, dated 2026-04-09, amount not shown on the public page); Dealroom lists a $125K seed and StartupHub $12M, which conflict. Patricia Tani is added as co-founder per Futurism.
